event.title: Trump Signs Executive Order on Childhood Vaccine Recommendations
event.canonical_title: Trump Signs Executive Order on Childhood Vaccine Recommendations
event.summary: President Trump signed an executive order that modifies childhood vaccination recommendations by limiting the inoculation schedule to 11 vaccines and advocating for spacing out vaccinations. The order aims to provide parents with more choices, but health experts and pediatricians have expressed concerns that these changes could lead to confusion and increased vulnerability among children.

timeline.title: Trump Signs Executive Order on Childhood Vaccine Recommendations
timeline.summary: An executive order signed by Trump recommends administering childhood vaccinations in separate visits and splitting the MMR vaccine into three individual shots. This directive aims to enhance vaccine research and was previously blocked by a federal judge.
key_facts: Trump signed an executive order on childhood vaccine recommendations.
The order suggests separating the MMR vaccine into three shots.
It directs improvements in vaccine research.
The recommendation to administer vaccines separately was previously blocked by a federal judge.
